Question: Mrs. Walter gave an exam in a mathematics class of five students. She entered the scores in random order into a spreadsheet, which recalculated the class average after each score was entered. Mrs. Walter noticed that after each score was entered, the average was always an integer. The scores (listed in ascending order) were \(71,\) \(76,\) \(80,\) \(82,\) and \(91.\) What was the last score Mrs. Walter entered?
Solution:
An average of \(k\) integer scores is an integer exactly when their sum is divisible by \(k\). This lets us work backward from the total
\[
71+76+80+82+91=400.
\]
Let \(L\) be the last score entered. The first four scores have sum \(400-L\), which must be divisible by \(4\). Since \(400\) is divisible by \(4\), so is \(L\). Only \(76\) and \(80\) qualify.

Suppose \(76\) were last. Then the first four scores would sum to \(324\). If \(t\) were the fourth score entered, the first three would sum to \(324-t\), which must be divisible by \(3\). Because \(324\) is divisible by \(3\), this requires \(t\) to be divisible by \(3\). But none of the remaining scores \(71,80,82,91\) is divisible by \(3\). Thus \(76\) cannot be last.

The remaining possibility, \(80\), is achievable. The order
\[
76,82,91,71,80
\]
produces successive averages \(76,79,83,80,80\), all integers. Therefore the last score was \(\boxed{80}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
